name: Wen Xiaoqiong
current_role: Member of the Wen family group named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (SZSE: 300498); no executive role disclosed
profile: Wen Xiaoqiong (温小琼) is one of the Wen family members named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group, China's largest hog and broiler producer. Wens was founded by her father Wen Beiying (per press reports) in 1983. She was among the top pre-IPO individual shareholders and is a passive shareholder rather than a manager.
interesting_fact: Wens began in 1983 when Wen Beiying raised 8,000 yuan from seven village families in Xinxing, Guangdong to start a chicken farm; it became China's largest livestock company, listing in Shenzhen in 2015.
notes: Very private; no public profile. Listed among Wens actual controllers in the 2023 annual report. Only route is the Wens board secretary office (dsh@wens.com.cn). Hurun listing was shared with Chen Jianxing (also a listed controller).

name: Sun Fen
current_role: Member of the Wen family group named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (SZSE: 300498); no executive role disclosed
profile: Sun Fen (孙芬) is listed in Wens Foodstuff Group's annual reports as one of the Wen family members who are joint actual controllers of the company, China's largest hog and broiler producer. Her wealth derives from that shareholding; she holds no disclosed management position.
interesting_fact: Wens grew from a 1983 chicken farm funded with 8,000 yuan from seven village families in Xinxing, Guangdong into China's largest livestock group, listed in Shenzhen in 2015.
notes: Very private, no public profile; exact family relationship not confirmed in sources checked. Hurun listing shared with Wen Zhifen (Wens chairman/legal representative). Route via Wens board office.

name: Sir Rocco Forte
current_role: Chairman, Rocco Forte Hotels (London-based luxury hotel group; 49% owned by Saudi PIF since 2024)
profile: Son of Lord (Charles) Forte, Rocco Forte became CEO of the Forte Group in 1992 but lost it to Granada's £3.87bn hostile bid in 1995. He started again in 1996 with Brown's (London) and The Balmoral (Edinburgh), building Rocco Forte Hotels with sister Olga Polizzi. In 2023-24 Saudi PIF bought 49% at a ~£1.4bn valuation to fund expansion.
interesting_fact: After losing his father's empire in one of Britain's most bitter takeovers, he rebuilt a luxury group from scratch; in 2001 the Forte trademark was returned to him, and he and Olga Polizzi won the Cateys 2026 International Outstanding Achievement Award.
deep_cut_fact: He read modern languages at Pembroke College, Oxford, where he won a blue for fencing, and qualified as a chartered accountant in 1969 before joining the family business; he is also UK patron of Les Clefs d'Or, the society of hotel concierges.
notes: Media-friendly and outspoken (Brexit, UK tax policy); gives interviews regularly. Company press page blocks automated access; use the press/media section of roccofortehotels.com for the current PR contact. Head office 70 Jermyn Street, London (company office).

name: Guo Miaobo
current_role: Shareholder and acting-in-concert party of the controlling group of Guangdong Chant Group (SZSE: 002616); holds no position at the company
profile: Guo Miaobo (郭妙波) is the spouse of Chant Group chairman He Qiqiang and one of the parties acting in concert with the company's actual controllers (He Qiqiang and Mai Zhenghui), per the 2025 annual report. Chant, based in Zhongshan, Guangdong, started in gas appliances and has expanded into biomass and waste-to-energy power generation and industrial-park heat supply.
interesting_fact: Chant Group pivoted from making gas stoves and water heaters into environmental energy, operating agricultural-biomass power plants and waste-to-energy and heat-supply projects in China, a possible angle for an energy podcast.
notes: Private, non-executive; the 2025 annual report states she holds no post at Chant. Better interview target would be chairman He Qiqiang; route via the board secretary office (dmof@chantgroup.cn).

name: Sun Feng
current_role: Founder, Chairman, General Manager and Board Secretary, Suzhou Secote Precision Electronic Co. (SSE: 603283)
profile: Sun Feng (孙丰, b. 1978) founded Secote in Suzhou in June 2007 and still runs it as chairman and GM. Secote makes automated assembly and inspection equipment for consumer electronics makers and has expanded into semiconductor wafer inspection equipment. He and co-controller Zeng Hui are the company's actual controllers.
interesting_fact: Unusually for a listed-company chairman, Sun Feng also personally serves as Secote's board secretary, the officer responsible for investor relations and disclosure.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Secote he started out as a test engineer at Kunshan KONE Elevator (昆山通力电梯), then ran a small automation equipment factory in Suzhou's Wuzhong development zone.
notes: Since he is also board secretary, the securities office email (zqb@secote.com) reaches his own office. Low English-language profile.

name: Huang Bo
current_role: Sole shareholder of Hong Kong-registered Hanjia Development Ltd (漢加發展), which holds ~9.5% of Hangzhou Atexco (Honghua Digital, SSE STAR: 688789); no management role disclosed
profile: Huang Bo (黄波, female) is an investor whose wealth comes from her holding company Hanjia Development, the second-largest shareholder of Atexco, a Hangzhou maker of industrial digital inkjet textile printers and inks. Atexco is controlled by chairman Jin Xiaotuan; Huang Bo is a passive shareholder.
interesting_fact: Atexco makes digital inkjet printing systems that replace traditional screen-printing in textile dyeing, and in 2023 bought 67% of ink supplier Tianjin Jingli to integrate ink production.
notes: Atexco's 2025 annual report identifies 'Huang Bo (黄波) 女士' as sole shareholder of Hanjia Development (9.54%). Essentially no public profile; common name, so be careful not to confuse with others. Only route is via Atexco's securities office.
